name: Genco Shipping & Trading
evidence_status: Conditional valuation: aggregate broker fleet mark is allocated by carrying value; post-quarter cash is estimated
limitations: The $1.42bn June fleet value is inferred from management’s rounded 18% net LTV disclosure; per-vessel values are allocated by carrying value, not individual broker marks.
Genco Volunteer is added at its disclosed purchase price less the disclosed delivery-delay adjustment, rather than a new October broker appraisal.
The July–October operating cash bridge is estimated; the $50m July revolver draw and $0.80 August dividend are explicit.
Open-fleet scenarios do not reconstruct every vessel charter or derivative position.
The debt facility is modeled as a 2031 bullet; this is a liquidity schedule, not a covenant or refinancing forecast.
Drydock cash is normalized from management budgets rather than a vessel-by-vessel survey calendar.
No replacement fleet is assumed after existing vessels retire; scrap proceeds use a DWT proxy.
audit_notes: August 12 company release says 43 vessels and 4.935m DWT, while the company fleet list and Q2 pro-forma counts imply 44 vessels and about 5.117m DWT after Genco Volunteer. The model uses the named 44-vessel register and flags the conflict.
Aggregate broker value is reverse-engineered as (330.0m debt - 73.587m cash) / 18%, then allocated to the 43 June vessels in proportion to disclosed carrying value.
